transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-18 14:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Nora (AE), Samir (SE), Elena (CSM) - Redwood; Ben (CTO), Rhea (Platform Eng), Omar (Security), Lina (PM) - Margo Tech

Summary/Notes auto sections (may be imperfect):
- Quick overview of pilot goals: answer generation for support triage, average 150 tokens response, 90th pct latency goal ~350ms for critical path.
- Security: customer requests VPC private deployment and customer-managed KMS; audit log retention 1 year.
- Action items: runbook, perf spreadsheet, security pack review.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Nora: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll walk through the activation roadmap.
[00:12] Ben: Hi, Ben here. Sorry running a tiny bit late - all good now.
[00:16] Elena: Elena from CS, hey all.
[00:18] Rhea: Rhea here.
[00:20] Samir: Samir - I'll take the technical bits.
[00:23] Omar: Omar on security.
[00:25] Lina: Lina, product.
[00:27] Nora: Great. Goal for today: align on pilot scope, decide deployment model (hosted vs VPC/private), confirm security checklist items, and assign owners + timeline.
[00:35] Ben: To set context - Margo's using the model to power triage for incoming support tickets. Expected volume is modest to start, maybe 1500 queries/day, peak bursts to 400 q/min. Key success for us is latency under 400 ms p95 and cost under $0.002 per inference average, roughly.
[00:52] Samir: ok, that helps. For p95 400ms, we'd recommend for initial pilot a dedicated small GPU pool or a private VPC with pinned capacity - avoids cold starts and gives predictable latency. We can quantify later once we see token distribution.
[01:06] Rhea: Could you explain difference again between dedicated and private? We kinda conflate dedicated and private in ops.
[01:10] Samir: Sure. Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's infra - you get guaranteed throughput but still hosted by Redwood. Private (VPC) means the serving plane sits in your VPC, optional on-prem or customer-managed network; you control ingress, egress, and KMS. Since you mentioned KMS and audit retention, sounds like VPC might be what you want.
[01:25] Lina: We prefer the VPC option for compliance - Omar will speak about encryption rules.
[01:29] Omar: Yeah, our compliance stance: we need customer-managed KMS, full audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and data residency in us-west for PII workflows. Also, SOC2 attestation is required - we need Redwood's SOC2 artifacts and pen test summary.
[01:45] Nora: We have a SOC2 pack, pen test summary, and an architecture whitepaper. We'll share them after the call. Quick note - our VPC flow supports customer KMS integrations and audit forwarding; there are a few setup steps around VPC peering or PrivateLink and egress rules.
[02:02] Elena: I'll put the security docs link in the follow-up email and include the onboarding runbook.
[02:06] Ben: Great. On metrics - aside from p95 latency and cost, we'll evaluate contextual relevance and hallucination rates on a sample of 1000 queries. Lina will own quality metrics.
[02:17] Lina: Yep, we'll provide labeled examples and a few edge cases. Expect to send those by Thursday.
[02:21] Samir: Perfect. On the perf side, can you share expected sequence lengths? You mentioned 150 tokens earlier but payloads vary. If your prompts average 80 tokens and responses 150, that informs GPU selection and batching strategy.
[02:35] Rhea: Most prompts are ~60 tokens, but some include long conversation history, up to 400 tokens in rare cases.
[02:40] Samir: Ok, rare long tail. We can configure KV cache and prefix caching; we'll also look at quantization profiles to reduce memory if needed. For the pilot, I'm thinking an L4 class instance pool, maybe 2 nodes to start - gives headroom for bursts. We'll run a synthetic load test and then a real pilot.
[02:58] Ben: Sounds reasonable. Any impact on accuracy from quantization? We can't degrade triage quality.
[03:03] Samir: Little risk for our 8-bit quant profiles for many open models; we'll include that as an experiment in pilot and baseline against full fp16. We'll lock on accuracy thresholds before enabling aggressive quant.
[03:14] Omar: For KMS, we want envelope encryption where Redwood stores ciphertext but key material is in our HSM. Is that supported?
[03:20] Nora: Yes, our VPC option supports customer KMS with envelope encryption. We'll need IAM policies and shared secrets rotation plan.
[03:27] Omar: Also need proof that key material never leaves our control.
[03:30] Samir: We can provide architecture diagrams; there are a couple of network hops that are visible but key ops remain in customer KMS - we'll add diagrams to the security pack.
[03:38] Rhea: Network-wise, what does peering look like? We want minimal NAT egress costs.
[03:42] Samir: We support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for reduced egress. For the pilot, PrivateLink tends to be simpler to avoid wide-open routes. We'll include the PrivateLink config steps in the runbook.
[03:53] Lina: Timeline question - how long to get pilot up end-to-end?
[03:56] Elena: From experience, VPC pilot with KMS normally 2-3 weeks if security review is quick. Can be longer with slow approvals.
[04:04] Ben: We're aiming to have a pilot running by March 10. Is that realistic?
[04:08] Samir: If we get the prompts and security answers in the next week, yes. Key gating items: KMS setup, VPC peering/privatelink, and credential exchange.
[04:17] Nora: We'll commit to getting the onboarding runbook and SOC2 pack by Friday 2026-02-20.
[04:22] Omar: We'll review and get back with any blockers within 5 business days - initial look by Feb 26th.
[04:28] Ben: For success metrics - aside from latency and cost, we want to limit hallucinations under 7% on labeled set. Also track tokenized cost per conversation.
[04:39] Samir: Agree. We'll instrument the pilot to surface token counts and per-route latency, and push logs to your observability endpoint. Note that we can redact PII before logs leave the VPC if needed.
[04:51] Rhea: How about rollback/rollout? We want canary strategies.
[04:54] Samir: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency or errors spike. We'll draft a rollout plan in the runbook.
[05:03] Lina: Will there be a cost estimate for the pilot?
[05:06] Samir: Yes, I'll prepare a pilot perf and cost spreadsheet - includes token cost, instance hour cost, and buffer for bursts. Expect that in the deep dive.
[05:14] Nora: Quick recap of owners: Samir - pilot perf sheet and tech deep dive; Elena - invites and cadence; Samir & Nora - runbook and SOC2 pack; Omar - share KMS diagrams; Ben - approve metrics. We'll list these in the follow-up.
[05:29] Ben: One more question - do you support redaction hooks or client-side preprocessing? We might want to mask certain fields before sending.
[05:35] Samir: Yes, you can do client-side preprocessing, and we also support server-side pre-processing hooks in the VPC flow. We'll include an example snippet.
[05:44] Omar: Ok that's helpful. Also to confirm retention: audit logs 1 year but we might need 3 years for some cases. Can you support configurable retention?
[05:53] Nora: We can support configurable retention for enterprise plans - we'll flag this to the account team and include options in pricing.
[05:59] Elena: I'll schedule the technical deep dive for next week and send calendar invites.
[06:03] Lina: Thanks folks.
[06:05] Ben: Thanks everyone.
[06:07] Nora: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the runbook and links.

--- End of transcript ---
